individual_dispositions.text: An identity must be recognised, stated, remembered or carried across a difference of presentation. Even “A is A” makes a minimal journey: the second inscription is not the first inscription, yet the judgment identifies them. The copula keeps them together through the difference that gives the act of identification its work.
individual_dispositions.complete_paragraph: An identity must be recognised, stated, remembered or carried across a difference of presentation. individual_dispositions.actual_positive_operation: Two inscriptions are distinguishable presentations held identifiable by an act of copulation.

individual_dispositions.text: For self-knowledge, both sides of that question matter. A self must differ from itself in presentation to have something to recognise, and remain itself for the recognition to be self-knowledge. At the [subjective pole](../concepts/C01-Subject-Defined-Indefinability.md), the present act cannot be reduced to a finished self-image. Yet the changing image need not sever the identity it articulates. The copula is the capacity to cross this difference while keeping the seam available.

individual_dispositions.actual_positive_operation: Present self-knowledge identifies through a changing presentation while the determining act remains different from its image.
individual_dispositions.specific_stronger_inference_if_removed: A finished self-image would exhaust the current act of recognising it, or every altered image would sever self-identity.
individual_dispositions.necessary_information_if_removed: Nonobjectifiable act and continuing identity remain joined through their actual difference.

individual_dispositions.text: Consider two people with the same name. Repeating the name does not decide which person is meant. individual_dispositions.complete_paragraph: Consider two people with the same name. Repeating the name does not decide which person is meant. Conversely, a change of name does not, by itself, make its bearer another person. Naming therefore presupposes an individuation it cannot accomplish by the sound of the name alone. Beneath the name, [counting holds the unique instance being named](../sources/analytic-philosophy/kripke/kripke-1981-naming-and-necessity/NOTES.md). “Counting” here means distinguishing this occurrence from another, before an explicit numeral or a public name has been assigned.
individual_dispositions.actual_positive_operation: Distinct bearers can share a name, and a bearer can receive a changed name; pre-nominal individuation holds this occurrence.
individual_dispositions.specific_stronger_inference_if_removed: The name sound alone would individuate its bearer or make changed naming equivalent to a different person.
individual_dispositions.necessary_information_if_removed: Instance/name/circumstance and constitution versus later public usage keep their different offices.

Their equality does not abolish the difference through which it can be recognised. Predicative content and numerical identification remain distinct operations even where ordinary speech lets one word carry both. [Determination](../concepts/C03-Determination.md) gives each assertion its scope by discriminating the respect in which it applies.

individual_dispositions.text: Identification therefore joins three moments: **name, instance and circumstance**. The name makes a determination articulable; the instance holds what is being identified; the circumstance supplies the horizon in which the identification and its alternatives can be compared. Identity is name and instance proposed relative to circumstance. “Proposed” does not mean arbitrary. It means that a claim of identity has a place, a criterion and consequences for which it can answer.

It means that a claim of identity has a place, a criterion and consequences for which it can answer.
individual_dispositions.actual_positive_operation: Proposed identity has its actual name, instance, circumstance, criterion and consequence.

individual_dispositions.necessary_information_if_removed: Constitutional situatedness and warranted exact identification must be available together.

individual_dispositions.text: Context can disambiguate a scope that a bare formula has not settled. The question is not only which words occur but what this use of them expresses, who is speaking, and which possibility is being entertained. The circumstantial whole supplies an ordering within which particular distinctions are made. Someone can identify a remembered person, distinguish a fictional namesake and entertain an alternative history because the act holds the respect under which each is being compared.

individual_dispositions.actual_positive_operation: A use of a formula acquires determinate meaning through speakers, context and entertained possibility.
individual_dispositions.specific_stronger_inference_if_removed: A bare word string would determine its referent and modal respect without any circumstance of use.
individual_dispositions.necessary_information_if_removed: Remembered real person, fictional namesake and counterfactual variation need their different comparison scopes.

individual_dispositions.complete_paragraph: The `1–2–3` pass follows the persons in sequence. The `4–5–0` recognition pass voids their isolation, recognises their unity and returns the achieved account to the relation through which it arose. Context does not insert a fourth pronoun. It makes the three positions available together, including the activity by which they were distinguished. Their unity does not erase the first-person, second-person and third-person differences. This is why the two triads can be read as `3:3` and as `3:1`: the recognition pass gathers the preceding three as one act. Its operation is different from the `4:2` distinction between four explicate positions and two implicate poles.

individual_dispositions.complete_paragraph: [Lived first-person appearing, organising identity, self-image and whole-Self](../concepts/C35-Selfing-Self-Subjectivity-Self-Thing.md) have distinct offices within this recognition.
